topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, the scope of the cancer lecture series, and the specific learning outcomes for the session.

topics.label: Cancer Pathogenesis and the Origins of Oncogenic Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and explain the fundamental biological processes that generate oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the 'Bad Luck' Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the evidence for environmental causes of cancer in contrast to intrinsic random mutation or 'bad luck'.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Cancer Etiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious pathogens contribute to oncogenesis, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a model of pathogen cooperation and chromosomal translocation.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which physical and chemical mutagens cause DNA damage, particularly through metabolic activation and adduct formation.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Host Context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic factors and microenvironmental conditions that promote the proliferation and outgrowth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for Identifying and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the laboratory and observational methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and determine whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Conclusion and Risk–Benefit Perspectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising key themes and framing cancer prevention around daily risk-versus-benefit decisions.
